topicName: Workflow Callers, Inputs, and Secrets Inheritance
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Workflow Callers, Inputs, and Secrets Inheritance in GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Reusable workflows allow you to prevent duplication by centralizing CI/CD logic. Understanding how to structure workflow callers, pass strongly typed inputs, and handle secret inheritance is critical for building secure and scalable pipelines."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Creating the Reusable Workflow (The Callee)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To make a workflow reusable, it must be triggered by the workflow_call event instead of push or pull_request. You define accepted inputs and secrets in this trigger block."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"name: Reusable Build and Test

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      environment:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: "Target deployment environment"
    secrets:
      api_token:
        required: true
        description: "API token for third-party service"

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Build
        env:
          API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.api_token }}
          ENV: ${{ inputs.environment }}
        run: |
          echo "Deploying to $ENV using provided token...""},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Invoking the Reusable Workflow (The Caller)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"A caller workflow invokes the reusable workflow using the 'uses' keyword. The path points to the repository, file path, and tag or branch ref."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"name: Caller Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]

jobs:
  call-build-workflow:
    uses: octocat/example-repo/.github/workflows/reusable.yml@v1
    with:
      environment: "production"
    secrets:
      api_token: ${{ secrets.PROD_API_TOKEN }}"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Secrets Inheritance Rules"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Secrets are not automatically passed down to reusable workflows for security reasons. You must explicitly pass them or use the inherit keyword."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Explicit Passing: You map specific caller secrets to callee secrets manually, such as api_token: ${{ secrets.PROD_API_TOKEN }}."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Inheritance: You can pass all caller secrets to the called workflow automatically using 'secrets: inherit'."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"jobs:
  call-workflow-with-inherited-secrets:
    uses: octocat/example-repo/.github/workflows/reusable.yml@v1
    with:
      environment: "staging"
    secrets: inherit"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always specify explicit input types (string, boolean, number) in the workflow_call trigger to avoid runtime parsing issues."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prefer explicit secret mapping over 'secrets: inherit' when working with public repositories or untrusted workflows to strictly limit credential exposure."}]
